title: In-app API reference, warm migration from XCP-ng and rolling update enhancements

items.text: Rolling updates show live apt progress per node, with the apt output on screen when a step fails
Rolling updates can require an explicit approval before each node, from the wizard or the Task Center
Rolling updates honour the parallel migrations setting and spread evacuated guests by projected load and affinity rules
Finished rolling updates stay in the Task Center with their full log, and a cancelled run reads cancelled
Rolling updates reach nodes on their management address and no longer wait on Ceph for our own noout flag or unrelated warnings
The node update preflight reads the Proxmox repository fields correctly, so the enterprise-without-free-alternative check finally fires
XCP-ng pools can be connected directly through XAPI, next to Xen Orchestra
Warm migration from XCP-ng with CBT: full copy of a live snapshot, then delta passes over NBD until the cutover
XCP-ng Live mode is removed, it never worked. Use Offline or Warm
XCP-ng offline downloads survive a slow SSH poll and retry three times instead of deleting the partial file
Hyper-V: inventory in a single PowerShell call, wrong credentials shown as an authentication error, SMB disk paths resolved, retry on the right engine
Windows guests installed with Compact OS convert: the ntfs-3g system-compression plugin is installed by the preflight
Hyper-V and Nutanix guests keep their source CPU count and memory instead of 1 vCPU and 2 GB
Cold migrations to file storage write the converted disk once and need half the temporary space
Warm node preparation states that it needs Proxmox VE 9 instead of dumping an apt transcript
Consoles: fullscreen and scaling controls on VNC and SPICE, remembered per console kind
SPICE console: start, shutdown, stop and pause the VM from the toolbar, with automatic reconnect
noVNC no longer logs the keystrokes typed into a guest to the browser console
HA: a single orchestrator leader at a time, elected on the Postgres primary only, and no more read-only transaction errors on a hot standby
HA: the DRS page is populated from any node, metrics and recommendations are routed to the leader
HA: a long preflight returns its verdict instead of a false Orchestrator unavailable
DRS migrations left running after an orchestrator restart are settled automatically, and the task footer shows their real progress instead of 50 %
Site Recovery: a replication job continues past a failing VM and reports a Partially synced status with the failed VMs named
Site Recovery: a replicated VM carrying a Proxmox snapshot syncs again instead of failing on rbd File exists
PBS 4.x: package refresh, repository toggle, API token listing, S3 endpoints and prune jobs work again
Network Flows: configuring sFlow succeeds, reports per-node results and is re-applied after a node reboot; flows are attributed by guest MAC
Commas work in the default notification recipients, and a list saved glued by the semicolon workaround is repaired
The public API reference is rendered inside the product, under Settings, with Try-it on your own instance
Tooltips stay reachable on disabled buttons, so the reason a button is unavailable is readable

title: vDC storage policies, tenant VLAN networks and a complete Task Center

items.text: vDC storage policies: a policy on a connection and one of its storages carries read and write IOPS and bandwidth caps plus a quota for that tier, is assigned to vDCs, and is stamped on the disks a tenant creates, deploys, clones, restores, imports or moves, with per-tier usage bars and a one-click apply to existing disks

Tenant VLAN networks: a provider hands each vDC one or more VLAN ranges and a shared SDN zone, and the tenant then creates its own networks inside those ranges, self-service, with the tag allocated from its pool
Optional VMID ranges extended to vDC tenants on shared provider clusters, with the used-VMID scan resolved through the tenant's vDCs so uniqueness and the next free id stay correct across tenants
The tenants table shows the optional VMID range in its own column, sorted on the lower bound
Task Center: migrations to Proxmox were invisible and could not be cancelled. The page never read the migration jobs table, so the Migration filter it offered could never match anything

Task Center: logs for every job type, rolling updates and replication from the orchestrator, migrations from the task history, DRS rebuilt out of the UPID and Site Recovery from the per-VM results. Actions are routed per type and recovery executions are reported as Site Recovery instead of maintenance
The ProxCenter tab of the taskbar lists the same jobs over the whole history, and a double click opens the Task Center

Warm migration nodes are prepared by the product: Broadcom closed the public VDDK download in August 2026, so the plugin ships from a private registry and a Prepare the node action installs nbdkit, nbd-client, the VDDK plugin and the symlink Proxmox 9 needs, idempotently

The operator chooses the warm cutover moment: in manual mode the run keeps issuing delta passes, one per minute with no expiry, until the switchover is asked for, and the downtime shown at the moment of the click is the real one

A warm cutover whose guest refuses to shut down is recoverable: the wait is a step of its own, restates the time left every minute and offers a hard power off, with the budget raised from 5 to 30 minutes. vSphere faults now carry what was actually refused
The warm downtime budget is settable from the migrate dialog, a curated slider paired with an exact seconds field over the 30 s to 24 h range the API enforces

virt-v2v no longer prompts for the root filesystem: a btrfs guest with snapper snapshots inspects as one system per subvolume, and the detached conversion died on end of file after the whole transfer had completed
A migration that failed between reserving a VMID and creating the guest no longer destroys a pre-existing VM holding that id

A datacenter declaring many PBS storages no longer renders an empty Target Storage field: the hardcoded 8 s read budget becomes a setting, the dialog surfaces the server reason with a retry, and a response timeout no longer reports a healthy but slow cluster as unreachable
VMID availability is scoped to the target connection, so cloning a template with two clusters connected works again instead of suggesting an id and then refusing it
Site Recovery: a powered-off VM can be selected for replication, and a tag-based job no longer silently drops one from its protected set while reporting success

A tag-based replication job whose tags currently match no VM reports the explicit no_match status instead of failing and mailing, with its next sync still scheduled. RPO alerts deliberately keep firing, because a job protecting nothing must keep nagging
The boot screenshot delay on a test failover is configurable from 5 to 600 seconds, so a guest that boots slower than the old 45 s constant is no longer photographed mid-boot
A DR test can leave the recovered NICs connected, with a warning about colliding production addresses, and the mode the run used stays visible on a chip

Alerts on replication RPO drift and Ceph OSD latency, the RPO grace expressed as a percentage of each job's own target rather than a fixed delay. The OSD check ships disabled, since no latency threshold suits every disk

A cleared alert sends a recovery notification carrying when it fired, when it cleared, how long it lasted and the value it came back to. Resolution waits for a configurable hysteresis, so a value oscillating around its threshold no longer mails once a minute
Alert mails keep the severity the engine established, so an alert with no measured quantity, such as a failed replication job, reaches an operator whose minimum severity is critical

Community installs grant the super-admin role again: since v1.4.7 an account created from Settings, Security, Users received no RBAC grant at all and saw an empty dashboard. Accounts already created without a grant are repaired at sign-in, the LDAP provisioned ones included

API tokens: the user dialogs list the tokens an account minted and offer to delete them while disabling or deleting it, deleting a token removes the row instead of stamping it revoked, and the creator is frozen on the token so provenance survives
A user whose only grant is a pool or a tag can create a guest again: the pool and storage pickers came back empty, the node picker had nothing to offer and the submit itself was refused
Creating an alert now requires the alerts.manage permission, and upload progress is readable only by the user who opened the transfer

A White Label primary colour typed without its leading hash no longer turns every page of the tenant into a 500, login page included, and an instance already stuck recovers on its own instead of needing a database edit

Security: the orchestrator no longer trusts X-Forwarded-For blindly on every request, where any caller could pick the IP it was recorded as (GO-2026-5777), and it builds on a Go toolchain that still receives patches
Disk health on the node view: SMART attributes per disk, including the NVMe text form real hardware returns, plus ZFS pool state, scrub and vdev tree
Node temperatures read from the kernel hwmon tree over SSH, aggregated per role with a threshold per role, next to the CPU, memory and root filesystem figures they measure
A ZFS ARC dashboard widget with its own auto scaled axis and a percentage view, since ARC flattens onto the baseline when it shares an axis with total memory
Disks report their real format instead of raw, and the Cloud-Init drive is labelled as such instead of appearing as a CD-ROM that the ISO editor could have detached

Removing RAM from a running guest no longer reports a failed save: PVE sleeps 3 s per DIMM, so the write outlived the request budget while PVE applied it. Config writes now follow the asynchronous PVE task, and the message names the stop and start a pending change needs
Backup jobs can follow a Proxmox resource pool, and the inventory panel resolves the pool members instead of showing a dash
The PBS token setup guide recommends DatastoreReader plus Audit: without Audit, server status, services, disks and update information stay empty
Dashboard widgets stay where they are dropped, and a theme-logo widget joins the library with the branding logo, the ProxCenter logo or the theme badge
The colour scheme is stored in the user account, per tenant and per user, and resolved server side, so a browser that clears cookies on exit no longer resets the theme
Text stays readable on a light branding colour, in the command palette, the profile button and the compliance report cover
The tooltip hover band on bar charts follows the theme instead of painting a white block over the hovered bar in dark mode

title: Authentication fixes, revocable sessions, disaster recovery failback

items.text: Security: an API path containing a dot no longer skips authentication. The middleware treated any dotted path as a static asset and answered before the session check, so a cluster with an FQDN node name exposed guest notes and task data to unauthenticated callers (GHSA-79j6-v2r5-5pw5)

Security: the guest notes, tasks and features routes now carry their own permission checks, evaluated before the Proxmox connection is resolved, so a refused caller never causes the stored API token to be decrypted

Security: the first-run setup endpoint is rate limited, accepts an optional shared secret, and decides that no account exists inside a serializable transaction, so two concurrent bootstraps cannot both create an administrator (GHSA-qxgh-pw46-6pw6)
Revocable server-side sessions: review and revoke your own sessions from a session management screen, and revoke someone else's from the admin user view. Idle and absolute lifetimes are configurable
Read-only API tokens: pxc_ tokens grant scoped, quota-limited access to aggregated public endpoints, for dashboards and external monitoring

Site Recovery failback: a reverse incremental sync brings the source back up to date, then an operator-driven cutover switches back, with per-VM rollback and re-protect. Failed-over plans stay locked until failback completes

Boot screenshots on a test failover: each recovered VM's console is captured while the test runs and kept with the execution, so you can see what a guest actually booted into instead of trusting a power state
Point-in-time recovery and configurable snapshot retention on replication plans, with per-VM failover steps shown on the execution results
A real failover fences the source VMs before starting their replicas, so the same guest cannot run on both sides
A failover no longer erases the recorded IP of a node that stopped answering
The orchestrator fails over to another node of the cluster instead of dying with the one it was configured with, and addresses guest commands to the node that actually owns the guest
Several vDCs per tenant, with a global vDC context to switch between them
Optional VMID ranges for MSP tenants
Tag and pool scoped users see their guests again: an account whose only grant was a tag or a pool saw an empty inventory since v1.4.6
Warm migration of large guests: a vSphere snapshot task is followed to completion instead of failing at a fixed 120 second deadline
Pre-migration check for HA resource affinity rules, so a guest bound by an affinity rule is caught before the move starts
Warm migrations warn before falling back to CBT, and report live progress during pre-zero and copy instead of showing an indeterminate bar
A fully copied warm target is kept instead of being freed when cleanup runs
Migrated Windows guests boot from SATA instead of LSI SCSI
The i440fx machine type is sent as pc, which unblocks guests pinned to that chipset
Custom CPU models are handled in the CPU type selects and in the cross-cluster migration pre-check
Migrated disks can optionally be converted to qcow2
Migration jobs orphaned by a server restart fail cleanly instead of staying stuck as running
The virt-v2v temporary storage requirement is hidden in warm mode, where it does not apply, and no longer reports a false lack of space
vzdump archives are listed in a guest's Backups tab
Security groups can be attached to guests, with a corrected membership count
The Proxmox rule log level is exposed in the firewall dialogs and rules tables
Firewall data is read directly from Proxmox when no orchestrator is running
A CIS Controls v8.1 card joins the compliance Frameworks tab
Reports carry the tenant's white label, including the compliance PDF export, its logo and its footer
The infrastructure report includes every VM instead of stopping at a cap
AI prompts are answered in the language of the interface, whichever provider serves them
A provider-configurable maintenance banner can be broadcast to every tenant
The PVE node is shown in filtered flat VM lists, and console windows lead with the VM name
Numeric fields can be cleared instead of snapping back to a default while typing
Snapshot rows follow the Proxmox task instead of claiming success before it finishes

The tasks bar keeps the content reachable when it expands, dashboard widget filters stay reachable when a filter empties the view, and batch actions stay available when alerts are selected from the header checkbox
A tenant selector on the storage overview lets a provider read one tenant's storage without leaving the page

title: Control-plane HA, warm migration reliability & license add-ons

items.text: ProxCenter HA (required license): turn a standalone installation into a three-node control plane with replicated PostgreSQL, etcd quorum and a virtual IP that fails over
HA deployment wizard and cluster dashboard: guided conversion with prerequisite checks and live progress, then per-node status, service grid and operations panel
Branding and login assets are stored in PostgreSQL, so logos and login backgrounds are identical on every node of an HA cluster
License add-ons: option licenses stack on top of your edition license, appear in the license table with their capabilities, and are available from the customer portal
Interactive warm cutover: choose the cutover moment with a live downtime estimate instead of letting the migration switch over on its own
Delete all snapshots of a VM in one action, with a guard that blocks a cross-cluster migration while snapshots still exist
Batch acknowledge and delete on alerts: select several alerts and act on them in one go
Blueprints gain custom images, cloud-init configuration, hardware sliders and IP and bridge selectors
Inventory and topology trees and the connections list are scoped to RBAC infrastructure grants, so a user only sees the connections they were granted
Korean and Spanish interface languages, and KRW currency support
VMs attached to SDN VNets are grouped by VNet, with VXLAN and zone information
Cloning suggests the next available VMID instead of a random one
The external hypervisor VM table can be sorted by column, which makes picking guests out of a large vCenter inventory practical
Users created on a Community installation are granted full super-admin rights
Remaining hardcoded French strings in the alerting UI moved to translation keys, so the interface is consistent in every language

Warm migration allocates block volumes as raw instead of qcow2, which removes a large allocation delay on LVM and Fibre Channel targets, and a failed allocation no longer leaves an orphan volume that poisons every retry
Warm migration allocates a free NBD device instead of assuming one, so a second concurrent migration no longer collides
Warm copy over SSH keeps the connection alive and applies an inactivity timeout, so a long copy can no longer hang indefinitely
A cross-cluster migration no longer fires two destroy tasks on the source VM, which could report a spurious failure after a successful move
Node Local Time no longer applies the UTC offset twice in the inventory
Storage capacity in the Overview is aggregated per cluster, so shared storage is no longer counted once per node
The SSH-command and task-log copy buttons fall back gracefully when the browser blocks the clipboard API outside a secure context
The migration log console keeps its last line visible above the tasks footer
A scheduled backup job runs on the guest's real node instead of the first node of the cluster
Cloud-init IP settings are applied on bridges that have no IPAM configured
VM names starting with a digit are accepted
Host VLANs with no attached VM are shown in the inventory Network view
The generated PVE token setup script includes Sys.PowerMgmt, so node reboot and shutdown work without editing permissions by hand
Panel width is remembered and theme status chips are readable in both light and dark themes
Sorting external hypervisor VMs no longer crashes on incomplete inventory data
Security: node, VMID and storage identifiers are validated before being interpolated into SSH commands
Security: the license client no longer keeps the previous entitlement state when a license check fails, and falls back to Community instead

title: Compliance frameworks, DRS load balancing & OIDC role fix

items.text: Security compliance frameworks (Enterprise): assess a connection against NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, CMMC Level 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 from a new Frameworks tab, with a score donut, satisfied / partial / failed breakdown, per-node results and a styled PDF report
Open in Proxmox: a button next to the cluster or node name opens the native Proxmox web interface in a new tab, deep-linking a member node to its own management IP
The migration target-network selector now lists SDN VNets alongside classic bridges, so nodes whose guest networks are VNets no longer get an empty list
Inventory Network view shows host bridges and VLANs per node, so clusters with no VMs are no longer empty; bridges open a detail panel and SDN VNet ids resolve to their friendly alias
Node maintenance is simpler: entering maintenance triggers Proxmox node-maintenance (HA guests evacuated by Proxmox) with a note that non-HA guests must be migrated or shut down manually

DRS now honors the Balance Types setting (previously a dead knob): load-balancing candidates are filtered by guest type for both reactive balancing and homogenization, with a guest-type gate applied at execution time
DRS settings cleanup: removed the dead balancing-method and balancing-mode knobs, guarded balance-types at a minimum of one, one-row resource weights, and status icons on exclusions and balance-types
The inventory tree expand/collapse state is now scoped per tenant, so switching tenant no longer carries over the previous expansion
The cluster SSH test shows the per-node ok / error breakdown on failure too, not just on success
The VM delete confirmation dialog spells out exactly what will be removed

OIDC role preserved on login: v1.4.4 demoted OIDC users with no IdP group match to viewer on every sign-in (locking out manually assigned admins); the re-sync is now authoritative only when a group-to-role mapping is configured and groups are sent
OIDC accounts are labelled correctly and can no longer be given a local password, closing a credentials login path that would bypass SSO and MFA
Warm and direct-ESXi migrations preserve the source NIC MAC, so the migrated guest keeps its network identity instead of stranding its IP on a ghost adapter
Warm migration reliability: a stale /dev/nbdN device is released before attaching and the delta-apply is chunked under the SSH argument-size limit
Migrating a running LXC container now uses restart mode instead of online=1 (which Proxmox rejects for containers), so an online CT migration no longer fails outright
Dropped the misleading "vSAN datastore detected" log line on the vCenter migration path
The percent chart Y-axis is widened so the "100%" label is no longer clipped
Old completed tasks are no longer re-alerted as new events about a week after they ran
Security: patched Go orchestrator CVEs by bumping golang.org/x/crypto, x/net and x/sys (SSH, HTML and IDNA advisories)
Header tenant switcher with per-tenant dashboards for MSP: switch the active tenant from the navbar and see dashboards scoped to that tenant
Shared migration tasks in the footer, visible across users so the whole team sees in-flight migrations, with a warm-setup docs link
VM console screenshots are served as JPEG instead of raw PPM, for lighter and faster previews
RRD performance charts show dates on the axes for multi-day timeframes, not just times
The Backups tab surfaces the real gateway error instead of failing with "Unexpected token '<'" when a proxy returns an HTML error page
A failed migration block-device transfer is reported as a failure instead of being masked as success
Warm migration to a thick target bounds the zero-fill so it can no longer exit on a false ENOSPC
Guest and node API routes no longer swallow real errors, so failures surface instead of empty data
OIDC users re-sync their role from IdP group membership on every login, so group changes take effect immediately
RRD performance graphs are scoped to the resource rather than the whole connection, closing an RBAC scope leak
The inventory NETWORK section stays stable when a connection briefly blips instead of collapsing
Replication writes the DR config with cp -f on pmxcfs, avoiding a transient failure window
Security: removed the unused npm from the runtime image, patched dependency CVEs (undici, OpenSSL on the orchestrator) and refreshed front-end dependencies

title: MSP mode, multi-license stacking & connection diagnostics

items.text: MSP mode: an MSP tenant can own entire Proxmox clusters (full-cluster view) alongside vDC / IaaS slicing; the provider / NOC sees the whole fleet for supervision and license aggregation
Provider provisioning of connections to MSP tenants from Settings, with a Tenant / vDC ownership column and an owner selector when creating a connection
MSP tenants get fleet-wide scope on their owned clusters: inventory, dashboard, alerts, reports, backup jobs and VM migration among owned connections

Multi-license stacking: import additional licenses to grow fleet capacity without regenerating the primary license, with fleet-total quota, per-tenant rollup, Licensed-to per import, edit-mapping and remove
Connection health diagnostics: a per-connection column and modal running read-only reachability, auth, version, cluster / Ceph, storage and SSH checks; works in Community mode
Guest names in VM and CT alerts and event emails: the guest name shows next to the vmid in the alerts table, the navbar dropdown and the email template
Connections Nodes column collapses to the first node plus a count, with the full list on hover
Deploy wizard exposes real bridges and an editable VLAN tag for provider and MSP modes
Green Score insight moves to its own row so longer suggestions stay readable
The What's New panel no longer opens automatically on a new version; open it any time from the profile menu

Orchestrator API authentication now reads PROXCENTER_API_API_KEY (the value docker-compose injects), so auth can be enabled and matches the frontend; an unset key keeps auth disabled as a safe fallback

title: Warm migration, SPICE consoles, Ceph topology & security

items.text: Warm migration for VMware with changed-block tracking and a final delta sync: no data loss on large or busy disks, for ESXi-direct and vCenter (including vSAN), single and bulk, with a go/no-go preflight
In-browser SPICE console for QEMU VMs, alongside noVNC
Ceph CRUSH topology view in the cluster Ceph tab: read-only CRUSH tree with details and pools
Clone a VM from a snapshot restore point, choosing a snapshot as the clone source
Role-level default RBAC scope, inherited by every assignment of that role
SSO-only login policy for OIDC (hide the local form, force the SSO redirect)
Local TOTP two-factor authentication with an admin enforcement policy
Local migration from the cluster Guests tab (node-to-node), not just cross-cluster
Reports and notifications: connection scoping, backup report polish, per-category severity, and an event-email rework (English copy, task-log details, one mail per event)
Ceph tab shows the full cluster config with working OSD flag toggles
Dashboard widgets honor the appearance settings: font-size, corner-rounding and a shared gauge
Guest VLANs resolved from host bond sub-interfaces so tagged guests group correctly
Backups show the real local backup time with Proxmox-style columns; the empty Backups tab explains why
Security hardening: TOFU host-key verification, per-connection ws-proxy TLS, dependency advisories cleared, Node 26 pipeline hardening
Partial-VM cleanup no longer leaks the target VMID after a failed conversion
Grant Sys.Modify in token setup, with an actionable Rolling Update permission warning
Backups 'Run now' works again (a missing route returned an HTML 404)
VM User role gains the read access the Inventory needs to load
Standalone hosts behind NAT: node management connects to the public host, not the private interface
Serial and headless VMs show a badge instead of looping on a failing screenshot
Resume paused VMs; allow dots in tags; the guest icon dims when off; tree sections stay open on header click

title: MSP / IaaS — vDC, IPAM, PBS multi-tenant & Postgres

items.text: vDC tenant cockpit (My vDC) with live consumption: hosts, VMs metrics, donut quotas (CPU, RAM, Storage, Snapshots, Backups), datacenter map and green KPIs
Cloud-style tenant deploy flow with quota enforcement on every step (template, ISO, clone, restore)
Native IPAM at the vDC level: SDN VNet/subnet management, automatic IP/MAC reservation on deploy, clone, qmrestore and config edit, plus PVE pool scan to merge externally created VMs
Per-vDC PBS bindings with auto-provisioning of namespace, sub-token, ACL and PVE storage; manual mode also supported
Tenant restore from PBS: overwrite source VM or restore as a new VM into the tenant vDC pool, with simple-mode dialog
PVE backup jobs scoped to tenant pools, with structured schedule picker (frequency, time, weekdays) and Verify / Delete actions
Datacenters, country and Green IT configuration: per-datacenter assignments tree, country flags on tenants and clusters, green factors per node
Tenant-scoped alerts, tasks, events and reports on shared-node clusters, with vDC report type gated to super-admin
Per-resource Failback toggle in the HA tab and refreshed HA UI
LXC network edit with IP, gateway and IPv6 fields; templates listed from any node hosting the storage
Cross-cluster offline migration shows real progress; choose target VMID for external migrations; VLAN tag applied on migrated VM NIC
WeasyPrint sidecar for scheduled report PDF rendering
Tenants 'Disabled' state renamed to 'Locked' with explicit semantics
RBAC grants are preloaded once per request, removing the N+1 in scoping helpers
Settings tabs are now scrollable on narrow screens; enterprise-only tabs are hidden in Community instead of greyed out
Alerts visibility for tenants is awaited consistently across every callsite (regression test added)
Tags persistence drops raw SQL placeholders and restores tenant scoping
vDC tenants can SSH on provider connections; restored VMs land in the tenant pool
Shared storages are no longer hidden from the tenant scope
VxlanTag is now allocated against the live PVE state (not just the local DB)
PBS timestamps drop milliseconds before being sent to PVE; backupId is parsed correctly when the namespace contains slashes
Network inventory: IP usage column, click-to-detail modal, no flicker
Cross-tenant isolation hardened on inventory, PBS backups and PVE backup jobs (tenant with zero vDCs is no longer treated as provider)

Database backend is now Postgres only. SQLite is no longer shipped or supported. Re-run the install script to upgrade (e.g. curl -fsSL https://proxcenter.io/install/community | sudo bash): it adds the Postgres service, generates POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the postgres_data volume. The frontend re-bootstraps its configuration via the UI on first boot.
Hyper-V migration — connect to Hyper-V hosts, browse VMs, and migrate to Proxmox via virt-v2v
Nutanix AHV migration — connect to Prism Central, download disks, and migrate to Proxmox via virt-v2v
vCenter migration — migrate VMs from VMware vCenter (in addition to direct ESXi)
Migration Dashboard — unified view with KPIs, recent jobs, and hypervisor logos
SSHFS Boot migration mode — near-zero downtime VM migration from ESXi
Dashboard overhaul — dark vignette widgets, new widget types, global time range picker
Multi-dashboard support — create multiple dashboards with tabs and drag-drop reorder
Auto-HA — automatically configure High Availability for VMs on clusters
Live VM screenshot preview — see a live console preview for QEMU VMs
Datacenter Settings tab — configure PVE tag styles, general options, and more
LXC template listing — browse available CT templates in the creation wizard
Markdown notes — render Markdown in VM, node, and cluster descriptions
Hardware System section — BIOS, Machine Type, Display, SCSI Controller management
Configurable energy currency for Green IT cost display
Rolling update reboot prediction and skip indicator in wizard
Tags now display with PVE colors, shapes (full/dense/circle), and responsive overflow in all tables
DRS recommendations grouped by cluster with balance graph in drawer
Expandable charts everywhere — CPU, RAM, Ceph, Storage, with proper axes
VM summary panel — vCPU count, disk list, storage usage bar via guest agent
HA inline selector, console OS overlay, and chart color improvements
Cluster view — HA & Ceph UI improvements, node trends, affinity rules
Backup job dialog redesigned with HA resource management
Taskbar always dark in light mode with Proxmox node icons
LXC containers — swap editing and disk display
Migration pipeline — virtio-scsi driver, NTFS dirty flag recovery, guest tools firstboot injection
Top Consumers widget now persists CPU/Memory tab selection across page refreshes
DRS notification bell now matches the Recommendations tab (validates stale entries)
VM migration dialog now correctly detects local vs shared storage from PVE API
Tag colors consistent with Proxmox datacenter.cfg color-map across all views
Security: updated vite 8.0.2 to 8.0.5 (3 CVEs patched)
Real-time network traffic visualization powered by sFlow and Open vSwitch
Sankey flow diagram — interactive Source → Application → Destination visualization with animated flows
Time series bandwidth charts per VM with InfluxDB storage
Top Talkers, Top Pairs, and Top Ports overview with click-through details
sFlow agent management — configure OVS sFlow directly from the UI
Configurable sampling rate with recommendations based on network speed
InfluxDB integration for historical time series data
Full German (Deutsch) translation — available in the language selector
Multi-tenant support — isolate and manage multiple environments from a single ProxCenter instance
Tenant management panel in Settings (super admin only)
Per-tenant data isolation — connections, VMs, and configurations scoped to each tenant
Seamless tenant switching from the dashboard
Bulk migration — migrate multiple VMs at once from ESXi or XCP-ng to Proxmox
Live migration support — migrate running VMs with minimal downtime
ESXi migration pipeline with disk download, conversion (qemu-img) and import
XCP-ng migration pipeline with XVA export and automated conversion
Real-time progress tracking per VM during bulk migrations
